name: IN-03
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+16 district lean paired with a Republican incumbent on the ballot
Stutzman's roughly three-to-one fundraising edge over Thompson
No public polls; prediction markets put Democratic upset odds near four percent
Democratic-leaning national environment narrows but does not close the gap
model.rationale: A sixteen-point Republican lean, an incumbent who has out-raised his challenger nearly three to one, and market pricing that gives Democrats only about a four percent chance all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and no polling or expert ratings suggest the national environment can overcome that combination.
model.watch: A large influx of Democratic outside spending or national polls showing a historic midterm wave could pull the expected margin into single digits.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 3rd District is firmly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly sixteen points toward the GOP. Marlin Stutzman, the incumbent, is running for re-election and has raised nearly a million dollars, far outpacing Democrat Kelly Thompson's roughly $347,000, though Thompson's haul shows the race is at least contested. Prediction markets give Thompson about a four percent chance of an upset.

No public general-election polling is available and no expert raters flag the race as competitive, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals. The national environment leans toward Democrats this cycle, which should narrow the margin somewhat, but a sixteen-point Republican lean plus incumbency is a steep hurdle. The forecast expects Stutzman to win comfortably, with a Democratic upset requiring a far larger national wave than current indicators suggest.
